input: Get a soil test done before planting season

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Whether they are testing one small garden bed, multiple zones, or a large plot changes how many samples are needed and the complexity of the process.
Knowing whether this is for personal use, a shared community garden, or a farm affects whose requirements and expectations must be met.
The planting season deadline varies by region and climate, which sets the hard deadline for when results must be in hand.
Budget determines whether to use a free cooperative extension service, a low-cost mail-in kit, or a full professional lab analysis.
What they intend to grow drives which specific nutrients and soil properties need to be tested — vegetables, fruit trees, and lawns have different needs.
Knowing what they want to do with the results — amend the soil themselves, hire someone, or simply have a baseline — defines what a complete job looks like.
Whether they already have a testing service in mind or need recommendations determines the very first concrete action to take.

gold.taskTitle: Get a soil test done before planting season
gold.taskDescription: Complete a soil test on the user's land in time to act on the results before planting season begins.

questions.title: How large is the area you need to test?
questions.description: Understand the size and number of distinct zones or beds to be tested, which determines how many soil samples to collect.

questions.title: What are you planning to grow in this space?
questions.description: Identify the intended crops or plants, since different plants require testing for different nutrients and soil properties.

questions.title: When does your local planting season typically begin?
questions.description: Pin down the hard deadline so there is enough lead time to receive results and make soil amendments before planting.

questions.title: What is your budget for the soil test itself?
questions.description: Determine whether to pursue a free extension service, an affordable mail-in kit, or a comprehensive professional lab test.

questions.title: Is this garden just for you or others too?
questions.description: Clarify whether this is a personal garden, a shared space, or a commercial operation, as this affects whose input and sign-off matters.

questions.title: What do you plan to do with the test results?
questions.description: Establish what success looks like — self-applying amendments, hiring a professional, or simply establishing a baseline for future reference.

questions.title: Do you already have a testing service or lab in mind?
questions.description: Find out if the user has a preferred provider or needs guidance on finding a local cooperative extension, mail-in kit, or private lab.
